title: Mint-debt hook denominates debt in USDS wei but mints phUSD 1:1, silently mispricing when USDS and phUSD decimals differ
description:
The hook accrues debt as `added = amount * ratio / 100` where `amount` is the raw USDS wei delta that arrived on BalancerPoolerV2. That number is then accumulated verbatim in `mintDebt` and, when `pull()` runs, fed directly into `phUSD.mint(recipient, debt)`. Nothing in the hook reads `decimals()` of either asset or scales between them. The entire debt accounting implicitly assumes 1 USDS wei = 1 phUSD wei.

USDS on Ethereum is 18 decimals; phUSD's decimals are whatever the deployer sets. The hook takes `phUSD_` as a raw IMintable in the constructor and accepts any token. If phUSD is ever deployed with decimals != USDS decimals (e.g. 6 decimals, matching USDC-denominated stablecoins), each unit of USDS dispatched mints 1e12 phUSD per unit of USDS wei — wildly over-minting phUSD and handing the recipient a massively inflated IOU. Symmetrically, if phUSD had more decimals than USDS, `pull()` would materially under-mint. Either way the hook's declared semantics (`ratio`% of dispatched USDS becomes a phUSD IOU) are silently broken because no unit conversion exists.
impact: Direct protocol-wide value leak on `pull()`. The phUSD recipient receives wildly mis-scaled tokens versus what the dispatched USDS amount justifies; if phUSD is listed in the sUSDS/phUSD Balancer pool that backs NFT holders, the recipient can dump the over-minted phUSD into that pool, draining the sUSDS side and destroying the BPT that collateralises NFT claims. The hook's docstring and implementation imply matching decimals as an undocumented trust assumption.
attack_path: Owner deploys BalancerPoolerMintDebtHook with `phUSD_` pointing at a phUSD contract whose decimals differ from USDS.
setHook binds the hook to BalancerPoolerV2; minters dispatch USDS (18 decimals) through the pooler.
Hook records debt += amount * ratio / 100 using USDS wei but treats that number as phUSD wei.
Recipient calls pull(); phUSD.mint(recipient, debt) materialises the wrong number of phUSD.
Recipient sells the inflated phUSD into the sUSDS/phUSD pool, draining sUSDS away from the protocol's BPT backing.
recommendation: Either (a) require in the constructor that `IERC20Metadata(phUSD_).decimals() == IERC20Metadata(USDS).decimals()` (the hook needs the USDS address to enforce this; currently it never references USDS directly), (b) scale inside `onDispatch` using the on-chain decimals of both tokens, or (c) document and hard-code a single phUSD decimals value and revert if the supplied phUSD does not match. Option (a) is the least-code change; any decimals mismatch should revert at construction.
